chunks: 26. And with the first chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon both of them, saying:
"Surely, the righteous deed goes to Paradise and prepares for its doer, just as a man sends his servant ahead to furnish for him."
Then he recited: "And as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, they prepare for their own souls" (al-Rum, 30:44).

key_terms.العمل الصالح: The righteous deed — refers to any good act performed with sincere intention for the sake of God
key_terms.غلامه: His servant/attendant — a young male servant sent to prepare a place for his master
key_terms.فيفرش: To furnish/spread out — from the root f-r-sh, meaning to lay carpets or furnish a place
key_terms.يمهد: To prepare/furnish — from the root m-h-d, meaning to lay out or make comfortable

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about righteous deeds going to Paradise?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that righteous deeds are personified agents that travel to Paradise ahead of their doer to prepare a place, much like a servant sent in advance to furnish a dwelling. He supports this vivid metaphor by reciting Quran 30:44, which affirms that believers who do good deeds are, in reality, preparing for themselves. This teaching was conveyed to Dawud ibn Farqad, a companion of the Imam, illustrating a common motif in Shi'a hadith where the afterlife consequences of deeds are described in tangible, relatable terms.
